script.base: Carolina is a 3-point favorite in a 39-point game, so the book expects a close low-scoring afternoon, Carolina about 21 and Philadelphia about 18, not a shootout and not a priced blowout. Jalen Hurts is out (calf) and Saquon Barkley is out (hamstring), so Philadelphia is Tanner McKee, who has no prior games in this pack, behind an offensive line missing Landon Dickerson with Drew Kendall questionable. Base flow: Carolina uses Chuba Hubbard, AJ Dillon out, to stay in front; Bryce Young still throws first to Tetairoa McMillan (31 targets, 310 yards, 328 air yards in weeks 2-4); Philadelphia cannot reproduce Hurts' deep air yards and has to live on short throws to Makai Lemon, Dontayvion Wicks, Amari Cooper and Dallas Goedert plus a Pierce/Bigsby committee. Pace stays modest.
script.flip1: Carolina scores early and the lead stretches past +3. Hubbard's carries rise and McMillan's second-half targets stall in a clock-kill. Philadelphia then has to throw, which lifts Lemon and Wicks attempt counts, but McKee against Carolina's 36% blitz (PHI EPA/db -0.21 when blitzed) keeps those yards inefficient. McMillan over is hurt on this flip; Lemon over can still survive on chase volume.
script.flip2: Philadelphia runs on Carolina's 5.51 YPC defense (14 runs of 10+ in four games). Pierce and Bigsby, with Barkley and Will Shipley out, eat the play count, McKee stays on schedule, and the game is tied late. Carolina then throws more, which helps McMillan, while Philadelphia dropbacks shrink and Lemon's 20.5 becomes a thin target-share bet.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and both overs lost. Carolina's tackle and guard group, Freeling doubtful and Moton and Lewis questionable, never gave Young a clean dropback, Philadelphia sat in the shell that produced McMillan's 17-yard game, and Hubbard's clock-kill made 64.5 too far inside a 21-point team total. On the other side Philadelphia never had to throw: Pierce and Bigsby ran at 5.51 YPC against Carolina, McKee handed off, and Lemon finished on the 14-yard side of his last four while Wicks, Cooper or Goedert took the few checkdowns. Weather was not saved and could have been the wind that kills both the deep shot and the short timing. That counter-case is why Lemon is a lean, not a strong, and why Hubbard was not added. It is not stronger than McMillan's target gravity plus two Philadelphia defensive backs out, so the strong leg stays and is flagged, not cut.
slip_story: One story only: a competitive 21-18 grind in CAR@PHI, not a shootout and not an early clock-kill. McMillan recyds over 64.5 is the Carolina first-read yardage leg against a secondary missing Bennett and Carter II. Lemon recyds over 20.5 is the Philadelphia short-area leg that replaces Hurts' deep game once McKee is pressured at a 36% blitz rate. They can win together if both teams throw at least a little inside the 39 total. Do not add a total under, a Wicks over that needs Hurts air yards, a Hubbard over that needs efficiency this offensive line and this 4.09 YPC run defense may not give, or any touchdown. Two legs, no parlay beyond that story.
